title: Class 11 Chemistry — Periodic Classification Study Guide
topicTitle: Classification of Elements and Periodic Table
notes: Modern periodic law states that properties of elements are periodic functions of atomic number. The table is arranged by increasing atomic number into periods and groups; blocks s, p, d and f indicate the subshell being filled. IUPAC groups are numbered 1–18.

Nuclear charge is +Ze. Inner electrons shield outer electrons; effective nuclear charge is often approximated as Z_eff ≈ Z − S, where S represents shielding. Across a period Z increases while shielding changes less, so valence electrons usually feel stronger attraction. Down a group, added shells and shielding change the attraction and increase the size of the valence shell.

Across a period, atomic radius generally decreases as effective nuclear charge rises; down a group it generally increases because a new shell is added. Cations are smaller than their parent atoms and anions larger. In an isoelectronic series, radius decreases as proton count rises. First ionization energy generally rises across and falls down, with subshell and pairing exceptions. Electronegativity generally rises across and falls down; it is a relative bonding scale. Metallic character generally decreases across and increases down.

Electron affinity is the energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron. Trends are irregular and sign conventions vary: some sources use negative values for energy released, others quote energy released as a positive electron-gain enthalpy magnitude. State the convention if using numerical signs. Explain trends using effective nuclear charge, shielding and shell number rather than memorized arrows alone.
Example: O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺ each have 10 electrons. Proton count increases from 8 to 12, pulling the shared electron cloud more strongly; radius decreases in the order O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺.
keyPoints: Modern periodic position follows atomic number, not atomic mass.
Across a period, increasing effective nuclear charge usually contracts atomic radius.
Down a group, added shells usually increase size and metallic character.
For isoelectronic ions, greater proton count means smaller radius.
Ionization energy and electron affinity have exceptions; explain trends with shielding and shell structure.
practiceQuestions: Explain why atomic radius generally decreases from Na to Cl but increases down Group 1.
Arrange N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻ and Na⁺ in increasing ionic radius and justify the order.
Distinguish nuclear charge from effective nuclear charge and describe shielding.
Describe general trends in first ionization energy, electronegativity and metallic character across a period.
summary: Periodic properties recur with atomic number. Trends reflect the balance of nuclear attraction, shielding and shell number; use these to justify comparisons instead of memorizing directions alone.
